conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed. The photon ambient space is complex vector-valued L² with second-variable-linear pairing ∫ conjugate(u)·v d³k. The momentum dot product extends complex-bilinearly, while fiber norms use the positive Hermitian pairing.
For k ≠ 0, n = k/|k| and P_T = I − nnᵀ. The value at k = 0 is immaterial in L². The polarization-frame obstruction concerns continuous real orthonormal frames on S².

Coordinates have length units, x⁰ = ct, and η = diag(−1,1,1,1). A₀ = −φ/c; a = A/√(μ₀ℏc); μ = mc/ℏ; g = q√(μ₀c/ℏ); D_a = ∂_a − ig a_a. Gauge transformations are a′ = a + ∂α and ψ′ = exp(igα)ψ. The Clifford relation uses −η.

The classical spinor is a smooth commuting C⁴-valued map. SI constants and charge are symbolic inputs; no numerical μ₀, measured charge, Grassmann calculus, or interacting continuum construction is adopted.

The photon smearing phase is exp(i|k|x⁰ − ik·x), with coefficient (2π)^(−3/2)(2|k|)^(−1/2). E = −∂₀A, so [A_i,E_j] = −i P_T,ij δ³ after spatial smearing. Fields are operator-valued distributions on the finite-particle domain.
The spatial Fourier transform uses exp(−ik·x) and inverse factor (2π)^(−3). G = 1/(4π|x|) is distributional at the origin; its displayed classical second derivatives apply only away from the origin.

The Coulomb solver uses jointly smooth periodic data on a nonempty open time interval times T_L³, L > 0. Neutrality is required at every time, the solution has zero spatial mean, and Fourier coefficients use L^(−3) times the integral over one cell.

The finite-mode bracket is the complex-bilinear extension of the real canonical bracket on R^(4N), N ≥ 1. z = x + iy and p = (Pˣ − iPʸ)/2; barred symbols are their conjugates. ℏ > 0 and the reduced bracket is {z_j, conjugate(z_k)}_D = −iδ_jk/ℏ.

The future null cone omits its apex and uses dν = d³k/(2|k|). Lorentz continuity uses the Euclidean matrix topology. Translation phases are exp(i(|k|a⁰ − k·a)), so the joint multiplier coordinates are (Σ|k_r|, −Σk_r).

Tests for F(h) are real, smooth, compactly supported and antisymmetric, with F(h) = ½∫F_ab h^ab. Spacelike separation means η(x−y,x−y) > 0 for every pair of support points. The bounded observable is W_Segal(√2 g_h), and the regional algebra is norm-closed and unital.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On H = L²(R³,d³k;C³), multiplication by P_T(k) = I − nnᵀ for k ≠ 0 is an orthogonal projection. Its range H_T = {u ∈ H : k·u(k) = 0 almost everywhere} is a closed positive Hilbert space, with two-complex-dimensional nonzero-momentum fibers.

Assume Countable Choice. For real j ∈ C_c^∞(R⁴;R³), the displayed projected shell coefficient g_j belongs to H_T. A_T(j) = a(g_j) + a†(g_j) is defined on the bosonic finite-particle domain and has test-topology-continuous matrix elements. With E_i = −∂₀A_i, [A_i(0,x),E_j(0,y)] = −i P_T,ij(−i∇_x)δ³(x−y) distributionally.

On an open U ⊆ R⁴, use smooth real potentials and gauge parameters and a smooth commuting complex spinor, η = diag(−1,1,1,1), A_a = (−φ/c,A), a_a = A_a/√(μ₀ℏc), μ = mc/ℏ, g = q√(μ₀c/ℏ), and D_a = ∂_a − ig a_a. The transformation a′_a = a_a + ∂_aα, ψ′ = exp(igα)ψ gives D′_aψ′ = exp(igα)D_aψ and f′ = f.

Assume Countable Choice. On K₀ = {ε ∈ L²(R³;C⁴) : −ε⁰ + n·ε_spatial = 0 almost everywhere}, Tε = ε_spatial − nε⁰ is bounded and onto H_T, and [ε,δ]_η = ⟨Tε,Tδ⟩₂. The radical is N = ker T = {b(1,n) : b ∈ L²(R³)}. K₀/N with its induced form is a positive Hilbert space isometric to H_T.

Assume Countable Choice. The action [s(p)] ↦ [Λs(Λ⁻¹p)] on square-integrable future-null-cone quotient sections with measure d³k/(2|k|) is unitary and strongly continuous in the stated matrix topology, as is its bosonic Fock lift. The translation lift has joint spectrum {(E,P) : E ≥ |P|}, vacuum value zero, and the displayed maximal energy and momentum multiplication domains.

Assume Countable Choice. For real compactly supported smooth antisymmetric h, F(h) = ½∫F_ab h^ab = −A_b(∂_a h^ab) = a(g_h) + a†(g_h) on the finite-particle domain. Its effective test is conserved, and the smearing is gauge invariant and Lorentz covariant. The displayed electric, magnetic and mixed commutators are derivatives of the massless causal commutator and have causal support; spacelike-separated compact test supports give commuting field strengths.

Assume Countable Choice. For real antisymmetric compact smooth tests supported in an open O ⊆ R⁴, W_O(h) = W_Segal(√2 g_h) is bounded and unitary, with the self-adjoint field-strength closure as its one-parameter generator. The norm-closed unital *-algebras generated in spacelike-separated open regions commute.

Assume Countable Choice and the stated SI conventions and jointly smooth periodic data on I × T_L³. The Hamiltonian multiplier imposes div π_A + ρ = 0, which in Coulomb gauge becomes −Δφ = ρ/ε₀. Neutrality is necessary at each time. If neutrality holds for every time, there is a unique jointly smooth periodic zero-mean solution with φ̂_k = ρ̂_k/(ε₀|2πk/L|²) for k ≠ 0, and the displayed longitudinal energy equals L³/(2ε₀) times the nonnegative Fourier sum.

Assume Countable Choice and the stated Fourier convention. The inverse Fourier transform of |k|⁻² is G(x) = 1/(4π|x|) distributionally. Thus P_T,ij(−i∇)δ³ = δ_ijδ³ + ∂_i∂_jG. Away from zero, ∂_i∂_jG = −δ_ij/(4π|x|³) + 3x_ix_j/(4π|x|⁵).
